concept.name: Session profile
concept.definition: A volume profile (or Market Profile) computed separately for each trading session, so that every day gets its own volume-at-price histogram with its own POC and value area. It is the standard per-day unit of profile analysis, with prior-session levels carried forward as references.
concept.intuition: Each session gets its own fingerprint of where business was done, and yesterday's fingerprint becomes today's map.
concept.mechanics: For each session boundary (e.g., exchange day or user-defined session), lower-timeframe or tick volume is binned by price; platforms render one histogram per session and derive session POC, VAH, and VAL, optionally with developing values in real time.
concept.failure_modes: Session definition is critical — 24-hour futures markets make 'the session' ambiguous (ETH vs RTH), and different boundaries produce different POCs and value areas for the same trading.
concept.misconceptions: Prior-session levels are references, not obligations; the common opener-relative-to-prior-value frameworks are checklists of tendencies, not predictive rules.
concept.example: Monday's session profile gives POC 4,512, VAH 4,524, VAL 4,500; Tuesday opens at 4,530 above the VAH, and the trader watches for acceptance above or rejection back into Monday's value.
